author: Bitly contributor (Codex)
about: A publisher generates a 101-article catalog, retires and restores one useful entry, then authorizes Dub to import it in the real 100-link batches. The legacy route reads a retained URL.

steps.name: Publisher opens an account and registers the Dub callback
The first article is superseded on the following day
Publisher archives the outdated first article
Publisher chooses to migrate the remaining catalog to Dub
Dub opens Bitly authorization for the registered app
Publisher signs in to the Bitly account
Publisher reads the Dub consent page
Publisher grants Dub access to the account archive
Dub exchanges the callback code using its real form request
Dub lists active groups and available custom domains
Dub offers the archive tags for import
Dub checks the importer endpoint allowance before queueing
Publisher realizes the old article still supplies useful citations and restores it
Dub imports its first 100 links with the fixed start-time cutoff
Dub resumes using the cursor Bitly returned and finishes the archive
A legacy visitor triggers Dub to resolve a retained archive link
A team member mistypes the stored access token while reconnecting
Dub reports the invalid account token
Correcting the account token restores the group selector
A bookmarked link absent from this account cannot redirect
The publisher retains the catalog while the next import is planned
Dub checks the retained catalog for its next import
